Retrieved 2026-07-19 via Exa full fetch. The Independent, published 2026-07-18 18:08 BST.

Burnham urged to stick to Labour manifesto on North Sea oil.
- Allies say Burnham intends a "dynamic" start Monday; Downing Street speech to set out plans for "breathing space" on cost of living and growth in every part of UK.
- Media reports: could involve approving new North Sea oil/gas drilling; Burnham said to be "open-minded".
- 2024 manifesto (Burnham promised to honour) said Labour would not issue new North Sea licences — they would "not take a penny off bills" or improve energy security while accelerating climate change.
- Green MP Adrian Ramsay (Saturday): "Andy Burnham says he takes the climate and nature crises seriously, but words are no substitute for action. With heatwaves causing deaths, wildfires and extreme weather across the country, approving new oil and gas drilling is exactly the wrong response and will do nothing to bring down energy bills."
- Enrique Cornejo, Offshore Energies UK: "While we use oil and gas, it is common sense that we prioritise our own production, our own jobs, value in our economy, delivered with lower emissions than imports."
- Amy Cameron, Greenpeace UK: new drilling would be "a massive own goal" while the UK was "literally on fire"; "...squeeze out the last few drops from a dying oilfield... would be sheer folly."
- Kemi Badenoch (BBC Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg): Burnham's comments "airy-fairy stuff"; "a people pleaser" rather than someone who would make "tough decisions". "What I'm not going to do is give Andy Burnham a blank cheque. This is a man who doesn't want scrutiny, he doesn't want anyone asking him tough questions, he just wants to be a people pleaser." Also: she would "score as many points as possible if it means the right thing for the country".
- Note: Conservative backing for more drilling helped Tories win first Scottish parliamentary by-election in almost 50 years last month.
